name: ur cutter prowess

winrate_basis.source: statistics_matchups(format=modern, archetype_a='esper blink', limit=60), committed verbatim at .protocol/raw-matchups.json; row opponent='izzet prowess' winrate=0.4587 over sample_size=322 matches, joined to 'ur cutter prowess' in that file's `aliases` map on the 2026-09-10 signature validation that the prowess labels are one archetype

primary_gameplan: High Noon blanks Cori-Steel Cutter, which is the card the build is named for: its Flurry trigger only fires on the second spell they cast in a turn, and under High Noon there is no second spell. Wrath of the Skies then sweeps the one-toughness board at X=1 or X=2 without ever needing to connect.
secondary_gameplan: Fatal Push and Solitude answer Slickshot Show-Off and Dragon's Rage Channeler on the spot, and Witch Enchanter destroys a resolved Cori-Steel Cutter, which is an artifact, and comes back every time Phelia attacks.
opponent_gameplan: Monastery Swiftspear and Dragon's Rage Channeler come down on turn one and grow every noncreature spell; Cori-Steel Cutter makes a prowess Monk each time they cast their second spell in a turn and equips it for free. Mishra's Bauble, Preordain, Lava Dart and Mutagenic Growth are the cheap spells that make all of that add up, and Lightning Bolt closes. Post-board Consign to Memory answers our enters triggers and Meltdown answers nothing we play, which is why they lean on Unholy Heat and Spell Snare instead.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: 10 of 10 pulled 2026-09-10 sideboards; counters the enters triggers on Solitude, Flickerwisp and Overlord
9 of 10 pulled sideboards; two damage, or six with delirium, at a deck of one- and two-toughness bodies
8 of 10 pulled sideboards; one mana counters Phelia, Emperor of Bones and our own High Noon
8 of 10 pulled sideboards; taxes High Noon and Wrath of the Skies on the turn they matter

stance_rationale: Cori-Steel Cutter and prowess both key off spell COUNT, not on any one card, so a symmetric cap costs them more than it costs us: they are casting three spells a turn off Preordain and Mishra's Bauble and we are casting one. Wrath of the Skies is the clean counter beside it, sweeping a one-toughness board at an X we pick.

opponent_plan.posture_why: One-mana creatures that grow on every spell, plus Cori-Steel Cutter tokens and Lightning Bolt reach, means they are counting to twenty rather than trading resources.

key_cards.why: Named verbatim in opponent_gameplan; makes a prowess Monk on their second spell each turn and equips it for free
Named verbatim in opponent_gameplan; a hasty one-drop that grows on every noncreature spell they cast
Kills any creature in our seventy-five for one mana once delirium is on
Taxes the High Noon or Wrath of the Skies turn we have to have

play_plan.keep: Two lands, a white source and a one- or two-mana answer, never a slow hand.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Turn two High Noon on the play, or Wrath of the Skies at X=1 on turn three.
play_plan.watch_for: Blue open for Spell Pierce before committing the sweeper.
play_plan.posture_why: Their damage compounds, so the first sweeper matters more than any threat we deploy.

survives_opposing_board.why: Spell Pierce taxes it two and Consign to Memory cannot counter it - Wrath of the Skies is a white spell, not a colorless one, and its energy payment is a cost rather than a triggered ability. At X=1 it sweeps Monastery Swiftspear, Dragon's Rage Channeler and every Monk token.

Spell Snare counters it on the stack, which is removal rather than a blank, and once resolved nothing in their pulled 2026-09-10 board destroys an enchantment - Meltdown names artifacts and Into the Flood Maw bounces a creature. A resolved copy turns Cori-Steel Cutter's Flurry trigger off permanently.

self_cost: High Noon caps both players at one spell each turn. That costs us the Ephemerate-plus-creature turn and the evoked-Solitude-plus-two-drop turn, which are two of the three lines this deck wants on turns three and four, and it makes a hand of cheap interaction much worse. It is correct anyway because their curve is one mana and ours is two.
